newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Balcerowicz to advise on Bulgarian reform.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Balcerowicz to advise on Bulgarian reform.

text.p: Leszek Balcerowicz, the former finance minister who used tough shock therapy to restructure Poland's embattled economy in the early 1990s, has promised to advise Bulgaria on its urgently-needed reforms.
"Petar Stoyanov asked me to Bulgaria to share my experience in economic restructuring," Balcerowicz told PAP news agency after meeting Bulgaria's president in Warsaw late on Thursday.
Balcerowicz, 50, now head of the opposition Union for Freedom (UW), said he would not take a job in Bulgaria but saw it as his moral duty to help.
He will have his hands full in coming months as his party campaigns for parliamentary elections due in September.
According to PAP, Balcerowicz said Bulgaria should start by drawing up a list of its top economic problems and should overcome its food shortages by privatising agriculture.

The liberal Polish economist, as a member of the first Solidarity government after the 1989 fall of communism, launched reforms that overcame hyper-inflation and, removing subsidies to industry, laid the basis for a market economy.

Unlike Bulgaria, which delayed fundamental reforms for seven years, Poland is now enjoying one of the highest economic growth rates in Europe although many Poles recall the first reforms as a frightening time of hardship in which real incomes dropped and unemployment rose sharply.
